entries.claim: The called Per Dominum section supplies conclusion line 96 and response line 97. Lowercase r. is initial formatting, uppercase R. marks Amen; neither is a Latin word.

entries.claim: The direct secret body calls $Per Dominum; the exact shared conclusion and Amen have a separate declared dependency.

The shared Father-directed formula supplies conclusion words w020–w040 and response w041 Amen. It does not print the proper body or by itself establish response participation. House accents, ligatures, tuum: Qui and terminal Amen. are declared in the transcript.

The Benziger Brothers 1962 Editio iuxta typicam page, printed p. 467, leaf n548, prints the 19-word Secret body and the cue Per Dóminum; the 41-word witness explicitly expands Rubricae generales 115 a, including Amen. This states current conformity, not original transcription genesis.

The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.
